title: ESSAY 15: The Future of Rural Banking in India

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established under the RRB Act of 1976 following the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group.
NABARD acts as the apex institution for financing, regulating, and promoting agriculture and rural development in India.
RRBs operate under a unique ownership model: Central Government (50%), Sponsor Bank (35%), and State Government (15%).
Digital transformation through Banking Correspondents (BCs), Micro-ATMs, and UPI integration is essential for modernizing rural credit.
Addressing non-performing assets (NPAs) and structural capital deficiencies is critical to achieving long-term viability in rural banking.

blocks.content: Rural banking is not merely about extending credit; it is the cornerstone of sustainable inclusive growth and rural economic empowerment in India.
